$comment: Machine-readable defect manifest (ADR-0051). The startup banner reads this and names what is live at the running tag. Prose registry: apps/docs/mvp/defect-registry.md in the book repo.
summary: The decision endpoint exists and is wrong in two independent ways, with nothing in the repository capable of catching either. This is the tree chapters 2 and 3 examine.

defects.title: Precedence collapse: an inherited deny beats a grant written on the person
defects.detail: PermissionService.DecideAsync flattens the subject's own grants and every grant on every role they hold into one list, then applies deny-overrides across the whole list. The specification's tier table is not implemented: an explicit Allow on the user loses to an inherited Deny (AC-3), and depth is discarded entirely, so a nearer grant does not beat a farther one (AC-4). Written by the agent unprompted on all ten runs of the build task at claude-opus-4-8 with no rails and no specification. The comment above the code argues for deny-overrides on safety grounds, which is the industry prior the specification deliberately contradicts.

defects.title: Audit fidelity: a denied decision is recorded as allowed
defects.detail: The audit write records Allow whenever the engine returned Deny, and passes every other outcome through untouched. The decision returned to the caller stays correct, so the service behaves properly and lies only in its own record. Exactly one entry is written per decision, which is why the double-write shape of this defect class is absent here and this one is the wrong-outcome shape. Seeded deliberately: ten runs of the build task produced no instance of it. The line carries a comment naming itself.

defects.title: No gates of any kind
defects.detail: No tests, no CI, no analyzers, no architecture rules, no rails. Nothing in the repository is capable of catching a defect. This is the state chapters 1 through 4 describe, and it is deliberate. The first gate arrives in chapter 5.

defects.title: Audit entries are freely mutable
defects.detail: AuditLogEntry and DecisionAuditEntry both expose public setters on every property, and nothing prevents an update or a delete. An append-only audit log is a rule that exists only in prose at this tag. Note that append-only would not have caught H1B-AUDIT-FIDELITY: that entry is false when written, not altered afterwards.

defects.title: Role graph has no depth cap
defects.detail: A role may name a parent role with no bound on inheritance depth. The traversal added by the harvest task does terminate, because it keeps a visited set that stops cycles and diamonds, so the loop-forever risk carried by earlier tags is closed here. No limit on legitimate depth remains.
